It must leave topology, spatial points, address/node maps, biomes, player state, bases, active galaxy, markers, counts, and all unrelated system/planet fields unchanged. Its galaxy-qualified `name_index` maintenance prunes only stale aliases, preserves valid representatives, and deterministically fills missing keys; tests validate reachability/validity without promising a collision winner. ## Contract readback

NF-01 through NF-06 deliver an opt-in runtime observation type, extractor, and model application method, not automatic name integration. `DiscoveryNames` has two public maps keyed by canonical `SystemId` and `(SystemId, planet index)`; values are literal strings, where an empty present value clears and an absent key preserves. It is runtime-only and does not alter `SaveUpdate`, serialization, or the cache schema.

The extractor uses `ValidatedSave::discoveries()` so each raw record is paired with the address validated before typed deserialization. It maintains separate first-key-seen sets for system and planet records; a first row reserves the key even when `DM.CN` is absent, null, or non-string. Only exact SolarSystem and Planet types participate; unknown types reserve nothing. It preserves exact first-row strings, including empty strings, and never re-decodes packed addresses or infers a parent system from an orphan planet.

The model method changes names only on existing genuine systems/planets and updates both flattened and nested planet copies. It ignores missing targets and explicitly marked placeholders, never creates/promotes systems, and reports whether a value actually changed. It must leave topology, spatial points, address/node maps, biomes, player state, bases, active galaxy, markers, counts, and all unrelated system/planet fields unchanged. Its galaxy-qualified `name_index` maintenance prunes only stale aliases, preserves valid representatives, and deterministically fills missing keys; tests validate reachability/validity without promising a collision winner. The key easy-to-miss failure is clearing one duplicate name must not erase another still-valid system's alias. Existing cold extraction remains unnamed; required23 owns application integration and required24 owns the original export proof.
